description: A comprehensive, enterprise-grade Data Structures and Algorithms curriculum implemented natively in C. Designed for computer science students and engineering professionals. Covers memory allocation, pointer mechanics, linear/non-linear structures, binary trees, BST, AVL trees, heaps, hash tables, graphs, shortest paths, a dedicated Master Class segment on all Sorting Algorithms, Big-O complexity, and modern algorithm design paradigms.

institute.name: Coder & AccoTax
institute.author: Sukanta Hui
institute.location: 25(10/A) Shibtala Road, PO – N. C. Pukur, Barrackpore, West Bengal, India

subject: Data Structures & Algorithms (C)

teacher.name: Sukanta Hui
teacher.bio: Deeply passionate about memory management, procedural optimization, data structures, and computer science fundamentals in C and C++.

segments.title: Segment 1 - Linear Data Structures & Memory Foundations
segments.summary: Master fundamental dynamic memory management in C, dynamic arrays, pointer arithmetic, singly/doubly linked lists, stacks, queues, and deques.

modules.title: Array Data Structure, Dynamic Arrays & Matrix Algorithms
topics: Contiguous memory layout and indexing mechanics in C
Pointer arithmetic and array element access formula
Dynamic array resizing with realloc(), malloc(), and free()
Multi-dimensional arrays and Row-Major vs Column-Major ordering
Sparse matrix representation and matrix multiplication algorithms

modules.title: Singly, Doubly & Circular Linked Lists
topics: Node structure design with C structs and self-referential pointers
Singly Linked List insertion, deletion, reversal, and cycle detection (Floyd's algorithm)
Doubly Linked List node memory management and bidirectional navigation
Circular Linked Lists and applications in round-robin scheduling
Polynomial addition and sparse polynomial manipulation using linked lists

modules.title: Stacks, Queues & Priority Buffers
topics: Stack ADT: Array-based vs Linked List-based LIFO implementation
Infix to Postfix/Prefix conversion and expression evaluation engine
Queue ADT: FIFO mechanics, linear queue limitation & array shifting problem
Circular Queue using modulo arithmetic in fixed arrays
Double-Ended Queue (Deque) and Priority Queue basics

segments.title: Segment 2 - Non-Linear Data Structures, Trees & Hashing
segments.summary: Explore hierarchical data structures, binary trees, self-balancing search trees (AVL), heaps, priority queues, and hash table collision resolution.

modules.title: Binary Trees, BST & AVL Self-Balancing Trees
topics: Tree anatomy: Root, leaves, height, depth, subtrees, and binary tree properties
Recursive and iterative tree traversals: Inorder, Preorder, Postorder, and Level-Order
Binary Search Tree (BST) insertion, search, and predecessor/successor deletion
AVL Trees: Balance factor analysis and Single/Double Rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL)
Tree visualization and height calculation algorithms in C

modules.title: Heaps, Priority Queues & Huffman Coding
topics: Binary Heap representation in 1D arrays (parent/child index math)
Heapify-Up and Heapify-Down algorithms for Max Heap and Min Heap
Priority Queue implementation backed by Binary Heap in C
Heap Sort algorithm and runtime performance comparison
Huffman Coding tree construction for data compression

modules.title: Hash Tables, Collision Resolution & Hash Functions
topics: Hash functions: Division method, Multiplication method, and Mid-Square method
Collision resolution by Separate Chaining using linked list buckets
Open Addressing techniques: Linear Probing, Quadratic Probing, and Double Hashing
Load factor management, dynamic re-hashing, and performance analysis
Building a fast string-key hash dictionary in C

segments.title: Segment 3 - Graphs & Algorithmic Paradigms
segments.summary: Master graph representations, traversal algorithms, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, searching mechanics, and algorithm design paradigms.

modules.title: Graph Representations, Traversal & Shortest Path Algorithms
topics: Graph representations: Adjacency Matrix vs Adjacency List in C structs
Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS) graph traversal
Topological Sorting (Kahn's algorithm & DFS stack approach)
Minimum Spanning Trees: Kruskal's (with Disjoint Set Union) and Prim's Algorithm
Single-Source Shortest Path: Dijkstra's Algorithm and Bellman-Ford Algorithm

modules.title: Algorithm Design Techniques: Greedy, DP & Backtracking
topics: Greedy Paradigm: Fractional Knapsack, Activity Selection, and Greedy choice property
Dynamic Programming: Memoization vs Tabulation, 0/1 Knapsack, and LCS
Backtracking Paradigm: State-space tree exploration, N-Queens problem, and Maze navigation
Divide and Conquer paradigm: Binary Exponentiation and Matrix Exponentiation
Algorithmic trade-offs and complexity optimizations in systems programming

segments.title: Segment 4 - Master Class: Comprehensive Sorting Algorithms
segments.summary: A dedicated, exhaustive segment covering every major sorting algorithm family in C: Elementary Comparison Sorts, Divide & Conquer Sorts, Heap/Tree Sorts, Non-Comparison Linear Sorts, and Specialized Hybrid Sorts.

modules.title: Elementary Comparison Sorts: Bubble, Selection & Insertion Sort
topics: Bubble Sort mechanics and early exit flag optimization for nearly sorted data
Selection Sort minimum element scanning and minimal swap property
Insertion Sort online sorting mechanics and shift vs swap comparisons
Stability, best/worst case Big-O analysis, and space complexity comparison

modules.title: Divide & Conquer Sorts: Quick Sort & Merge Sort
topics: Quick Sort partitioning strategies: Lomuto vs Hoare scheme in C
Pivot selection strategies (First, Last, Random, Median-of-Three) to prevent O(n^2) worst case
Merge Sort recursive divide-and-merge process and guaranteed O(n log n) stability
In-place vs O(n) auxiliary memory trade-offs and cache locality analysis

modules.title: Tree & Priority Queue Sorts: Heap Sort & Tree Sort
topics: Heap Sort: In-place max heap construction and root extraction phase
Tree Sort: Building a Binary Search Tree (BST) and Inorder traversal extraction
Auxiliary space analysis (O(1) Heap Sort vs O(n) Tree Sort)
Priority queue extraction sorting pattern in C

modules.title: Non-Comparison Linear Sorts: Counting, Radix & Bucket Sort
topics: Counting Sort: Frequency array counting, prefix sums, and O(n + k) linear sorting
Radix Sort: Least Significant Digit (LSD) sorting using Counting Sort sub-routine
Bucket Sort: Distributing elements into floating point bucket buckets
Breaking the O(n log n) comparison lower bound: Conditions and memory trade-offs

modules.title: Specialized & Hybrid Sorts: Shell Sort & TimSort Principles
topics: Shell Sort: Diminishing gap sequence insertion sorting (Knuth vs Shell gaps)
TimSort Principles: Combining Insertion Sort runs and Merge Sort for real-world data
IntroSort: Hybrid Quick Sort + Heap Sort + Insertion Sort used in C++ std::sort
Comprehensive sorting selection decision matrix for enterprise applications

segments.title: Segment 5 - Output Tracing Lab & Capstone Projects Hub
segments.summary: Put your knowledge into practice with output tracing labs, pointer defect analysis, and industrial-grade C capstone projects.

modules.title: Output Practice Lab: Pointer Tracing & Memory Diagnostics
topics: Predict output of complex pointer arithmetic and array access expressions
Trace linked list loop mutations, stack frame allocations, and recursion limits
Diagnose dynamic memory leaks, dangling pointers, and double-free bugs
Analyze tree traversal outputs and stack state sequences
Evaluate sorting step-by-step trace and pivot selection states

modules.title: DSA Capstone Projects Hub: Industrial C Implementations
topics: Project 1: Custom Heap-Backed Dynamic Memory Pool Allocator
Project 2: Doubly-Linked List Undo/Redo Text Editor Buffer
Project 3: Graph-Based City Transit Navigation & Shortest Path System
